newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU monetary committee meets on markka ERM entry.
newsitem.headline: EU monetary committee meets on markka ERM entry.

text.p: The European Union's monetary committee met on Saturday to bring the Finnish markka into the exchange rate mechanism of the European Monetary System, a step towards joining an eventual single European currency.
"The meeting began shortly after 2 p.m (1200 gmt)," one EU diplomat told Reuters.

EU monetary sources said the meeting was not expected to last very long given expected broad support for the Finnish currency's entry into the ERM, which links most of the currencies of the EU's 15 states.
Stability among the bloc's currencies is a criterion for the single currency, due to be launched in 1999.

Swedish deputy central bank governor Lars Heikensten followed the tradition of the secretive committee and refused to say why he was in town. But he told Finnish journalists: "I hope to get home quickly."
Witnesses said the number of officials at the meeting was smaller than normal for such occasions, perhaps reflecting the essentially non-controversial issue of bringing the markka into the ERM.
In Helsinki, Finland Bank supervisory board member Anneli Jaatteenmaki confirmed the board had met on Friday and proposed to the government that the markka be linked to the mechanism.
"Yes, the meeting was held yesterday," she told Reuters by telephone. Asked what the central markka-ERM parity was, she said: "It is a secret decision".

Second finance minister Arja Alho made the proposal at an extraordinary session late on Friday night, Finnish radio said, adding that the supervisory board had voted by five to four in favour of the proposal.

The markka has been floating freely since September 8, 1992. It was briefly linked unilaterally to the European Currency Unit (Ecu) between June and November 1991, when it was devalued by around 12 percent and then re-linked to the Ecu.
But strong foreign exchange market speculation forced it further down in value, and it has since been left to float freely.
Finland's five-party coalition government, which is determined to be among the first countries to join a single currency, is responsible for the key decision on whether to seek a markka-ERM link.
Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto said on October 9 it seemed likely that belonging to ERM was an unconditional criterion for joining the third stage of EMU.
"The fact that the currency has been stable is hardly enough, but the general opinion ... is that ERM is a system which one must join," he said.
The EU monetary committee is made up of national treasury and central bank officials. The markka was trading at 2.986 to the German mark at the close of market business on Friday.
